prompt:
Create a clean technical engineering diagram for NVIDIA engineers and managers.
Core claim: Create a clean technical engineering diagram for NVIDIA engineers and managers. Core claim: DLSim-to-silicon correlation now needs state matching, not more profiling; the async state trace is the bridge between matching the OSL distribution and profiling only the matched runtime windows. Figure class: single-mechanism. Example mode: none. Use visual proof rather than explanatory prose. Show the claim with the smallest useful set of visuals: - a left-to-right pipeline from DLSim async RL operating points to NeMo-RL async Llama with matched OSL distribution, to async state trace capturing time-indexed runtime state, to offline window matching, to targeted profiling windows - a small status band that clearly separates landed work from remaining work Tracked entity and identity rule: - the same DLSim operating-point family should remain visually recognizable across the full flow; the tracked entity is the operating-point tuple family, not a code path Identity invariants: - keep the same 5-point DLSim operating-point family visible across the story - keep the same async generation-worker runtime state as the thing being traced - keep the correlation target from simulator to silicon unchanged even as the observability level increases Changing variable: - what changes is the observability level: global OSL distribution -> time-indexed runtime state windows -> matched silicon windows -> targeted profiling Visual invariants: - OSL distribution matching is shown as a completed prerequisite, not the final goal - the async state trace is shown as an additive extension of the existing async vLLM metrics path, not a separate system - profiling appears only after matching windows are identified - landed and remaining work are visually distinct - avoid code-level details and file names Measurement window: one async generation step or one runtime state window, not a whole training job Allowed labels and verified numbers: - DLSim 5 operating points - gen_batch_size - context_batch_size - gen_kv_slen - ifb_sample_weight - OSL distribution matched - state matching - targeted profiling - async state trace - existing async vLLM metrics path - landed - remaining Needed text: only the labels above plus a short title if needed Forbidden elements: - code paths - file names - low-level config fields - paragraphs - mini code blocks - unsupported metrics - cluttered dashboards Visual rules: white background, flat technical shapes, semantic colors only, minimum necessary text, no decorative slide styling. Constraints: 16:9.
Follow the proof grammar chosen by the prompt author instead of inventing a different structure.
Figure class: `single-mechanism`.
Example mode: `none`.
Use visual proof rather than explanatory prose.
Keep text to the minimum necessary: short labels, key numbers, and compact formulas only when they save words.
Prefer simple visual primitives such as comparison blocks, bars, small charts, heatmaps, timelines, queues, arrows, and grouping.
If the proof elements read like text cards, sentence-heavy stage boxes, or slide bullets, rewrite them as visual primitives instead of preserving that textual structure.
If the request contains more detail than the proof budget allows, simplify or omit lower-priority detail rather than cramming more panels into one figure.
Use only supported details from the source or reasonable visual inferences from those facts.
If a specific detail is uncertain, omit the unsupported detail rather than inventing it.
Include formulas only when they are source-backed and materially reduce explanation. Never invent equations or denominator text.
Avoid paragraph-like text, decorative slide styling, glossy gradients, hero cards, and KPI banners.
Figure-class guidance:
- Use one main mechanism, causal chain, or pipeline as the proof object.
- Keep at most one small inset if it directly clarifies the mechanism.
Complexity budget:
- 1 main mechanism
- at most 3 regions
- at most 4 numeric callouts
Example handling:
- Do not invent an example; stay with the direct source-backed mechanism or result.
Optional layout hint: `system-pipeline`.
Default visual rules:
- white or near-white background
- flat technical shapes
- semantic colors only
- no decorative slide styling
Use aspect ratio 16:9.
